findings.summary: The per-projection column kernels executed, but full-PDF performance stayed flat. Keep the retained 32-row/128-column decoder tiles.
observations: The paired full evaluator passed all 60 calls and 5,580 raw EOS checks. Candidate speedup changed −0.14% p50, +0.87% p95 and +0.53% throughput against the fresh control; these effects are within the observed repeat variation.
All three ordinary diagnostic calls and the separate full instrumented call passed. NACA median is 2.496 s: OCR 2.058 s and embedding 0.300 s. Mean shares are 82.7% OCR and 11.9% embedding.

Each GPU captured 2,336 smaller decoder matmul launches. Narrow projections now commonly use 32-block grids, while the earlier fixed-column trace commonly used 16. QKV/gate grids changed to 20/48 blocks at the corresponding decode size. The intended column choices therefore reached actual GPU execution.

The original fixed32 configuration had already improved p50, p95 and throughput materially. This additional column adjustment gives no clear full-PDF gain; larger launch grids alone do not establish a speedup.
The bounded capture includes vision prefill, and its kernel sums are not whole-call wall-time shares. Raw trace paths, block counts and grids are saved in decoder-kernel-execution.json.
findings.next_step: Restore the retained fixed32 configuration. Check compiled embedding batches around 16, using the existing frozen vectors and a repeated stage control; propose a full-PDF run only if that screen shows a useful gain.
findings.optimization: Embedding remains about 11% of NACA call time. Its earlier batch-size screen used eager execution, so the compiled configuration needs its own measurement.
